who: Historian of Arkansas at Arkansas State University, doctorate from the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville.

evidence.says: The C. Calvin Smith scholarship biography identifies his Arkansas doctorate, career at Arkansas State, retirement as distinguished professor in 2002, and work establishing Heritage Studies; his books include War and Wartime Changes and Educating the Masses.
The university history records Calvin Smith's appointment to its history department in 1970.
This Charles Smith candidate is Charles Lee Smith, a William Jewell history professor and Mercer College president.
The other Charles Smith candidate is Charles D. Smith, University of Arizona Near Eastern studies scholar and author of Palestine and the Arab-Israeli Conflict.
Crosbie Smith is the University of Kent historian of science associated with Energy and Empire, a different scholarly identity.

notes: The supplied candidates represent other Smiths; none identifies the Arkansas State historian C. Calvin Smith.

who: James Morton Smith, historian of early America, University of Wisconsin professor and State Historical Society director; PhD Cornell 1951.

evidence.says: The department lists Armand La Potin's Minisink Patent dissertation in 1973–1974 with advisor Smith, James.
The 1971 AHA program identifies James Morton Smith as director of the State Historical Society of Wisconsin and professor of American history at the University of Wisconsin.
The candidate's authority heading is Smith, James Morton; its references identify the Wisconsin Historical Society director and Cornell doctorate in American history and constitutional law, 1951.

notes: The abbreviated advisor name agrees with the candidate's institution, period and early American field.

who: David G. Haglund, Queen's University political studies professor specializing in international security and Canada–United States relations.

evidence.says: In the acknowledgements to The Same Yet Different, Bernard James Brister thanks David Haglund, professor at Queen's University, for challenging his arguments, alongside Royal Military College academics (PDF page 8).
The David G. Haglund authority identifies a Queen's University political studies professor and author of The U.S.-Canada Security Relationship and Sister Republics.

notes: Brister's publication of the named dissertation connects the advisor directly to the Queen's scholar; the Royal Military College student affiliation does not imply that Haglund was employed there.

who: Vĩnh Sính / Vinh Sinh, University of Alberta professor of Japanese history, PhD Toronto.

evidence.says: The Vĩnh, Sính authority includes the variants Vinh Sinh and Sính, Vĩnh and identifies the University of Alberta Japanese historian and editor of The Future Japan.
The 2004–2005 staff calendar lists Vinh, Sinh as professor of History and Classics, with MA and PhD from Toronto and an Alberta appointment beginning in 1983.

notes: The AHA name is reversed relative to the usual Vinh Sinh form; authority variants, Japanese-history field and Alberta appointment establish the match.

who: R. David Weber, recorded as Margaret Wilson's USC history-dissertation advisor in 1979; full identity unconfirmed.

evidence.says: The supplied candidate is Ronald Weber, Notre Dame American studies professor and author of The Literature of Fact and Hired Pens, with a Minnesota doctorate.
Notre Dame identifies Ronald Weber as its faculty member from 1963, American studies department chair during the 1970s, and scholar of American literature, journalism and culture.

A professional association identifies another history professor, Robert David Weber, whose principal teaching career was in the Los Angeles Community College District and who worked on Reference Service Press scholarship guides.

notes: No independent source located connects Ronald Weber to the USC dissertation. Robert David Weber is a possible alternative, but his supervision of Wilson was not established; leave the candidate match unresolved.

who: Gareth Williams, University of Michigan professor of Spanish and chair of Maximillian Alvarez's 2020 dissertation committee.

evidence.says: Michigan lists Alvarez's joint Comparative Literature and History doctorate and Technologies of Resistance dissertation with Gareth Williams as chair.
The Romance Languages and Literatures faculty directory identifies Gareth Williams as professor of Spanish.
The first candidate is Gareth Williams, MD, a professor of medicine and dean at Bristol, previously a diabetes researcher at Liverpool, associated with Textbook of Diabetes.
The second candidate is Gareth David Williams, Columbia University classicist and author of Banished Voices.

notes: Neither candidate is the Michigan Spanish professor: the authority records identify a medical scholar and a Columbia classicist.

who: Jonathan H. Zeitlin, Wisconsin–Madison historian and social scientist, later University of Amsterdam public policy professor; PhD Warwick 1981.

evidence.says: The university lists Mitchell Larson's Practically Academic dissertation in 2002–2003 with advisor Zeitlin, Jonathan H.
Zeitlin's institutional biography records eighteen years teaching at Wisconsin–Madison before January 2010, including a history professorship, and a Warwick doctorate in 1981.
The authority identifies Jonathan H. Zeitlin, Warwick social history PhD 1981, Wisconsin–Madison faculty member in 1991–2010 and subsequently Amsterdam professor.

notes: The university's explicit student–advisor listing and the authority's career facts agree.

who: Michael Idomir Allen, University of Chicago classicist and medieval historian, PhD Toronto 1994.

evidence.says: Michael Idomir Allen's CV records Chicago employment from 1996 and a Toronto medieval studies PhD in 1994; page 18 explicitly lists his supervision of Jeremy Thompson's Lupus of Ferrières dissertation.
The candidate is Michael Thad Allen, author of Engineers and Modern Managers in the SS and a Georgia Tech scholar of German history and the history of technology.

notes: The CV identifies the exact student and dissertation, establishing a different Allen from the candidate. It dates the supervision to 2014, while the AHA entry gives 2015.
